title: Middleware, CORS & Gzip
summary: Write custom middleware, configure CORS, and enable Gzip compression.

sections.content: Middleware runs AROUND every request: before and after. You can modify requests before they reach your route, and responses before they're sent to the client.

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
import time

app = FastAPI()

@app.middleware("http")
async def add_process_time_header(request: Request, call_next):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-Process-Time"] = f"{time.perf_counter() - start:.4f}"
    return response
Order of execution: middleware runs in reverse order of registration for the 'before' phase (last registered runs first).
CORS allows browsers to make requests to your API from a different domain. Configure it with CORSMiddleware:

from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["https://myapp.com", "https://admin.myapp.com"],
    allow_credentials=True,          # needed if browser sends cookies
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

sections.title: CORS security rule
sections.content: Never use allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True in production. Browsers reject it anyway. Always specify explicit origins.

from fastapi.middleware.gzip import GZipMiddleware

app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=1000)  # compress > 1000 bytes

sections.title: Middleware order matters
sections.content: Middleware is applied in reverse order of add_middleware calls. The last middleware added runs first on the request path (outermost layer).

quiz.question: When does middleware execute?
options: Both before and after (around the request)
quiz.explanation: Middleware wraps around the request: code before call_next runs before the route, code after runs after. It's 'around' the entire request-response cycle.

quiz.question: What is the correct CORS configuration for production?
quiz.explanation: Always specify explicit origins in production. Never combine allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True — browsers reject it.

quiz.question: What does GZipMiddleware do?
quiz.explanation: GZipMiddleware compresses response bodies larger than minimum_size (default 1000 bytes) using gzip, reducing bandwidth.

quiz.question: What is the order of middleware execution?
quiz.explanation: Middleware runs in reverse order of registration for the 'before' phase. The last middleware added is the outermost layer, running first on incoming requests.

quiz.question: What parameter do you need to call to pass the request to the next middleware/route?
quiz.explanation: Use call_next(request) to pass the request to the next middleware or route handler. It returns the response.
